events.title: The Daily Courant Launches in London
events.description: On March 11, 1702, The Daily Courant was first published on Fleet Street in London. It is regarded as England's first daily newspaper. It was a single-sheet paper that mostly carried news reports from abroad.
events.significance: It started the tradition of daily news in English and helped make Fleet Street the center of British journalism.

events.title: Sir Alexander Fleming Dies
events.description: On March 11, 1955, the Scottish bacteriologist Sir Alexander Fleming died at his London home at age 73. He had discovered penicillin in 1928. His ashes were interred in St Paul's Cathedral.
events.significance: Fleming's discovery of penicillin opened the age of antibiotics, and it has saved millions of lives.

events.title: Lithuania Declares Independence
events.description: On March 11, 1990, Lithuania's newly elected parliament voted to restore the country's independence from the Soviet Union. Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to take this step.
events.significance: The declaration encouraged independence movements across the Baltic states and the Soviet Union. It was an important step toward the Soviet collapse in 1991.

events.title: The Tōhoku Earthquake and Tsunami Strike Japan
events.description: On March 11, 2011, a magnitude 9.1 earthquake struck off Japan's northeast coast. It triggered a huge tsunami that devastated coastal communities.
events.significance: It was one of the strongest earthquakes ever recorded. It led to the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident and changed disaster preparedness and energy policy in Japan and elsewhere.
